Bad Trip
BAD TRIP
noun (Boomer slang)
From trip (a drug experience, American slang from the mid-1960s) qualified by bad. In the LSD culture of 1966–70 a bad trip was an experience of terror, paranoia, or panic under the drug, sometimes lasting hours and occasionally producing lasting psychosis; "bum trip" was a synonym. By the 1970s it was used figuratively of any frightening or miserable experience.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A bad trip was the dark side of the psychedelic experience: hours of panic, paranoia, hideous visions, the terror that one had gone mad and would never come back. The phrase then spread to mean any miserable ordeal. The Christian observation: the bad trip is not an accident of the drug culture but its confession. Every intoxicant promises one thing and delivers another, and Scripture had already written the review: "At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder" (Pro 23:32). "There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death" (Pro 14:12). Many of the Boomer generation came home from a bad trip changed — some broken, some sobered, some converted. In the Jesus Movement of the early 1970s, a striking number of testimonies began, "I was on a bad trip and I cried out to God." The Psalmist knew that cry: "I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears" (Psa 34:4). The fear of the bad trip is the fear of a mind left to itself, without anchor. God’s gift is the opposite: "God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2Ti 1:7). A sound mind is not the absence of experience; it is a mind held by its Maker.

Webster 1828 Definition

Boomer slang (mid-1960s) for a terrifying experience under LSD or another drug, hence any miserable ordeal — the bite of the serpent Proverbs promised at the last (Pro 23:32).

expand to see more

BAD TRIP, n. (Boomer slang, c. 1966–present) 1. A frightening, panicked, or psychotic reaction to a hallucinogenic drug. 2. fig. Any distressing or unpleasant experience. "That job was a bad trip." Syn. bum trip, bummer.

Webster (1828) — TRIP, noun A stroke or catch by which a wrestler supplants his antagonist. And watches with a trip his foe to foil. 1. A stumble by the loss of foot-hold, or a striking of the foot against an object. 2. A failure; a mistake. Each seeming trip and each digressive start. 3. A journey; or a voyage. I took a trip to London on the death of the queen. 4. In navigation, a single board in plying to windward.

Decode for families: when a grandparent says "that was a bad trip," he may be speaking literally. Ask gently.

Modern Corruption

The drug culture treated the bad trip as bad luck; Scripture treats it as the promised end of the way that seemeth right (Pro 14:12), and answers its fear with the sound mind God gives (2Ti 1:7).

expand to see more

The counterculture had an answer for the bad trip: better "set and setting," a calmer room, a guide, a different dose. It never asked whether the whole enterprise was the problem. Proverbs does: the drink that "moveth itself aright" in the cup "at the last ... biteth like a serpent" (Pro 23:32), and the deceived man still says, "I will seek it yet again" (Pro 23:35). The bad trip was not a malfunction; it was the bill.

Yet God used it. The terror of a mind coming apart drove many young people of that generation to the end of themselves, and there they found that the God of Psalm 34 hears. A father telling this story to his son need not hide the grandparent’s past; he can show how grace met it. The spirit of fear is not from God; power, love, and a sound mind are (2Ti 1:7).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Middle English badde + trip → mid-1960s LSD slang bad trip → figurative "any ordeal."

expand to see more

Middle English badde — evil, worthless (origin uncertain)

English trip — a journey; mid-1960s, a drug experience

c. 1966: bad trip / bum trip in the LSD culture

1970s: figurative — any frightening or unpleasant experience

Scripture: Pro 23:29–35 — the intoxicant that bites like a serpent
